description: Draft accessibility plan identifies city barriers.
Proposes actions to improve accessibility for residents.

chips.text: Approved
People with disabilities and older adults are the focus.
Consultation with deaf-blind community members is a potential limitation.
Delegate highlighted challenges with screen reader friendly surveys.
Consultations included deaf, Black, cultural, and Indigenous communities.
City plans accessibility audits and expert consultations.

segments.title: Introduction to Accessibility Plan
description: Online survey gathered community feedback for the plan.
Report to council due by December 3rd deadline.
Focus on community-driven understanding of accessibility barriers.
538 residents provided feedback on barriers and solutions.

chips.text: 538 residents
Report to council before December 3rd
deaf/hard of hearing, Black, cultural, Indigenous communities

segments.title: Built Environment - Indoor Spaces
description: First of seven domains, focusing on indoor accessibility.
Residents reported issues with navigation, doors, elevators, and washrooms.
City plans accessibility audits and improved design standards.
Staff training is needed for barrier removal.

chips.text: people who are deaf, hard of hearing, blind or have low vision
City planning accessibility audits and expert consultations

segments.title: Co-designing Accessibility Solutions
description: Committee member asked about including people with disabilities in design.
Speaker agreed on engaging in co-designing issues.
Community consultation will occur during design standard review.

chips.text: solution for one group of people can be still be a challenge for another group
engage in some consultation with community

segments.title: Built Environment - Outdoor Spaces
description: Residents highlighted issues with sidewalk ramps, snow, and road visibility.
Surface conditions, park access, and obstructions were also concerns.
City plans to improve snow clearing and expand sidewalk repairs.
Enhancing park accessibility and signage are also priorities.

chips.text: people with mobility challenges
City to update sidewalk bylaws and evaluate faster snow removal

segments.title: Information and Communication Accessibility
description: Community raised concerns about digital exclusion and changing technology.
City website issues and inaccessible documents were highlighted.
Staff training gaps and emergency contact confusion were noted.
City is developing a digital equity strategy and improving website accessibility.

chips.text: older adults are not necessarily have the same digital literacy as younger generations
City is doing a digital equity strategy

segments.title: Accessible Transportation
description: Residents identified issues with parking, pathways, and accessible taxis.
Concerns included transit vehicle availability and complicated booking.
Bus stops lacking shelters and unclear signage were also noted.
City plans to redesign bus network and improve accessible transit.

chips.text: people with disabilities
City is redesigning the bus network

segments.title: Service Animals Policy and Understanding
description: Residents expressed concerns about staff understanding of service animals.
Need for clearer policies and welcoming spaces was highlighted.
City plans to improve staff knowledge and uphold accommodation laws.

chips.text: City to improve staff understanding and policy clarity

segments.title: Accessible City Services and Programs
description: Residents found registration steps confusing and communication limited.
City websites were hard to use, and staff training had gaps.
Program access barriers and unclear purchasing processes were noted.
City plans to review services and improve programming access.

chips.text: City to review services through a lens of accessibility

segments.title: Inclusive Employment Practices
description: Residents found the application process difficult and accommodation unclear.
Some felt judged during hiring due to their disabilities.
City plans to improve inclusive job postings and hiring practices.
Ensuring a fair employment process is a key goal.

chips.text: City to improve inclusive job postings

segments.title: Addressing Attitudes and Biases
description: Residents reported staff treating people with disabilities as less capable.
Feelings of unwelcome and lack of understanding for non-visible disabilities.
City plans to increase understanding of respect and inclusion.
Improved training and accessible technology use are planned.

chips.text: City to increase importance of understanding of respect and inclusion

segments.title: Accessibility Plan Next Steps and Timeline
description: Plan to be approved by council by December 3rd deadline.
Community feedback collected until September 22nd.
Administrative and committee reviews before November 19th council date.
Overall feedback has been positive, with some changes made.

chips.text: Plan to be approved by council by December 3rd
Community consultation process is in place until September 22nd

segments.title: Motion to Receive Accessibility Plan Information
description: Committee moved to receive the accessibility plan information.
Feedback deadline for the committee is September 22nd.
The motion was adopted without opposition.

chips.text: Motion adopted
